text: The messy-combination problem from Lesson 1 could be patched a dozen ad hoc ways. This project doesn't do any of that. It builds a real, three-stage pipeline instead, the kind a Data Analyst is actually expected to reason about.

Stage one, T-SQL, pulls two focused extracts straight out of AdventureWorks2012. Stage two, Python, cleans and joins those two extracts into one reliable DataFrame. Stage three, Power BI, builds the model and both stakeholder pages on that single combined dataset.
Filtering, joining, and aggregating the source tables belongs in T-SQL. The database engine does it fastest, and it keeps each extract focused on exactly the rows and columns that question needs.

Getting two messy extracts into one clean, combined shape is exactly what pandas is built for. Dropna and fillna handle missing and inconsistent values, drop duplicates removes re-pulled rows, and pd dot merge joins the two extracts together on a shared key.
Next lesson starts at the very beginning of that pipeline: writing the two real T-SQL extracts against AdventureWorks2012.
